description_en: The pavilion (baiṭhak) is situated in Ajayamerukoṭa, north-west of Amargadhi, Dadeldhura's current headquarters. The pavilion is located by the side of the Ḍo Gāḍ river, at the foot of the hill of the fortress of Ajayamerukoṭa (DDL0180).The area of Ajayamerukoṭa is rich in monuments that were mostly erected during the 14th and 15th centuries. According to D. P. Ojha, Ajayamerukoṭa was a local capital of the Khasiya kings from Jumla, (i.e. the Khaśa Malla emperors, 12th-14th century) (Ojha 1989: 54). From the mid-14th century, Ajayamerukoṭa seems to have taken greater importance as a capital of the Doti kingdom, especially under the reign of king Niraya Pāla (r. c. 1362-1383 CE). Indeed, it is around Niraya Pāla's time that Doti emerged as an entity independant from the Khaśa Malla empire. This political and economical rise is demonstrated in the numerous monuments erected between the second half of the 14th century and throughout the 15th century.The Ajayamerukoṭa Baiṭhak is one of these monuments. It is built on a quadrangular stone platform. A stone pillar is placed on each corner. An additional pillar is placed between each corner pillars, thus making a a total of 8 pillars. The pillars support an entablement made of large stone beams, one on each side. On top of the entablement is a stone corbelled dome, identical to the one that used to crown the nearby Setibada Baiṭhak (DDL0050). D. R. Sharma names this pavilion Rājāko Baiṭhak (Sharma 2012: 317-318).The pillars display an array of finely carved decorative patterns. Each pillar has, in its upper section, a motif of pot (kalaśa), repeated on the four sides. The lower registers mostly contain the losange motif of "diamond" (ratna).South-east of the pavilion, between the monument and the river, stands a partially buried pillar (DDL0140-001), similar in style to the ones from the pavilion. This artefact either indicates that another monument, probably a pavilion, was built on the spot, or that it was brought here from a collapsed monument located elsewhere. Moreover, is very likely that a flood of the river at some point destroyed one or more structures built by the side of the river.Given the historical context of the area and its general style, it is possible to date the pavilion from approximately 14th-15th century.
description_ne: यो पुरातात्त्विक सम्पदा डडेलधुरा जिल्लाको सदरमुकाम अमरगढीबाट उत्तर-पश्चिम दिशामा अजयमेरुकोट भन्ने स्थानमा अवस्थित छ । अजयमेरुकोट ईशाको चौधौं र पन्ध्रौं शताब्दीमा बनाइएका सम्पदाहरूले धेरै धनी स्थान हो । डि. पि. ओझा (१९८९: ५४) अनुसार अजयमेरुकोट जुम्लाका खश मल्ल राजाहरूको स्थानीय राजधानी थियो । ईशाको चौधौं शताब्दीको मध्यतिर राजा निरय पालको समयमा (शासनकाल ई. १३६२-१३८३) डोटी राज्यको राजधानी भएपछि यो अजयमेरुकोटको महत्त्व झनै बढेको प्रतीत हुन्छ । निरय पालको आसपासको समयमै खश मल्ल साम्राज्यबाट डोटी एउटा स्वतन्त्र राज्यको रूपमा उदय भएको देखिन्छ । यो क्षेत्रमा निर्माण गरिएका पुरातात्त्विक सम्पदाहरूले यो राज्यको राजनैतीक र आर्थिक वैभवता आँकलन गर्न मद्दत पुर्याउँदछन् ।यो अजयमेरुकोट बैठक ढुङ्गाको आधारमाथि बनाइएको छ र बैठक संरचनाको हरेक कुनामा एउटा एउटा र सबै कुनाका थामहरू को मध्यभागमा एउटा गरी जम्मा ८ वटा ढुङ्गाका थामहरू ठड्याइएका छन् । थामहरूले ढुङ्गाका ठुला-ठुला दलिनहरूलाई थामेका छन् र त्यसमाथि ढुङ्गाकै गजूर छ । यो गजूरको संरचना नजिकैको सेतिबड बैठकको (DDL0050) गजूरसँग मिल्दोजुल्दो छ । डिल्लीराज शर्माले (२०१२: ३१७-३१८) यस बैठकलाई राजाको बैठक भनेर सम्बोधन गरेका छन् । माथि उल्लिखित थामहरूमा राम्रोसँग बुट्टाहरू कुँदिएका छन् । हरेक थामहको माथिल्लो भागमा (चारै पट्टि) कलशाकृति कुँदिएका छन् । प्रायः थामहरूको तल्लो भागमा भने  रत्नाकृति देख्न सकिन्छ । यो बैठकको संरचनागत विशेषता र यस क्षेत्रको ऐतिहासिकतालाई मध्यनजर गर्दै यो बैठकलाई ईशाको चौधौंदेखि पन्ध्रौं शताब्दीमा राख्न सकिन्छ ।
